skill.name: create-pr
skill.description: Automates GitHub pull request preparation by checking the current branch, summarizing changes, drafting PR text, pushing the branch, and creating a PR with gh CLI.
skill.summary: Prepare, push, and create GitHub pull requests from current branch changes.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or obfuscated payload was found in SKILL.md; the high-entropy alert is a false positive from readable Markdown and Japanese text. Most command detections are Markdown fences, inline labels, or fixed read-only git checks. The material risk is intended remote mutation through git push, gh pr create, and shell command substitution for the PR body.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before git push or gh pr create, and display the remote, branch, base branch, title, and body first.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution for PR body
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a reviewed body file or safe argument handling over inline command substitution with generated PR text.
Verify qa-check status, clean working tree, authenticated gh CLI, expected base branch, and absence of secrets before publishing.

content.user_title: Create GitHub Pull Requests from Code Changes
content.value_statement: Pull request creation can miss context, checks, and consistent wording. This skill analyzes branch changes and prepares a structured GitHub PR with gh CLI.
actual_capabilities: Checks the current git branch and warns when it is main.
Compares the branch with origin/main using commit logs, changed files, and diff stats.
Classifies changed files into backend, frontend, documentation, and other groups.
Drafts a PR title, structured body, checklist, test section, and issue reference.
Pushes the current branch to origin and creates a GitHub PR with gh CLI.
Reports the created PR URL, title, base branch, issue, and change summary.
limitations: Requires git, a configured origin remote, and an authenticated GitHub CLI session.
Assumes qa-check is complete and all changes are already committed.
Uses origin/main as the default comparison unless the user changes the workflow.
Does not resolve merge conflicts, failed authentication, or rejected pushes automatically.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a completed branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub pull request for my current branch against main. Summarize the changes and ask me before pushing.

prompt_templates.title: Include issue context
prompt_templates.scenario: Add issue linkage and QA status.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pull request for the current branch. Link issue 123 and include the qa-check results in the test section.

prompt_templates.title: Review before publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Draft first, then wait for approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the commits and changed files, group the changes by area, and draft the PR title and body. Wait for my approval before push or PR creation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a release PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with custom base branch and risk notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a review-ready GitHub PR against release/2026.07. Include risk notes, migration notes, screenshots, and use gh CLI only after I approve.

output_examples.input: Create a PR for a feature branch that adds profile settings.
output_examples.output: A GitHub PR with a feature title, backend and frontend summaries, test status, checklist items, related issue, and PR URL.

output_examples.input: Draft a PR description for a bug fix branch before publishing.
output_examples.output: A reviewable PR draft that explains the bug, changed files, validation steps, and open notes for the reviewer.

output_examples.input: Prepare a release PR with documentation changes.
output_examples.output: A structured release PR summary with documentation updates, change counts, checklist status, and next review steps.

best_practices: Review the generated title, body, base branch, and remote before approving any push.
Confirm qa-check passed and the working tree is clean before creating the PR.
Check that no secrets or internal-only details appear in the diff or PR body.
anti_patterns: Running the workflow from main or from the wrong feature branch.
Allowing automatic push and PR creation without reviewing the generated content.
Using the workflow with uncommitted changes, unknown remotes, or an unauthenticated gh CLI session.

faq.question: Does this skill create the pull request automatically?
faq.answer: It can push the branch and run gh pr create after preflight checks. Users should approve those actions first.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on gh CLI for PR creation and PR viewing.

faq.question: Can it work outside GitHub?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow targets GitHub repositories and GitHub Pull Requests.

faq.question: Does it run quality checks?
faq.answer: No. It assumes qa-check already completed and records the reported test status in the PR body.

faq.question: What repository data does it inspect?
faq.answer: It reviews branch name, commits, changed files, diff stats, and generated PR text.

faq.question: Why does the audit recommend caution?
faq.answer: The workflow can publish commits and create a remote PR. Those actions should require clear user approval.
